key: Heaven and earth do not act from (the impulse of) any wish to be benevolent; they deal with all things as the dogs of grass are dealt with.
s: The chapter says heaven and earth act from no wish to be benevolent, dealing with all things as dogs of grass; Wang Bi, on chapter 5, reads it as heaven and earth following what is so of itself, making and doing nothing while all things order themselves: earth grows no grass for beasts, yet beasts eat grass.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 5, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

opened.locator: chapter 5, comment on 天地不仁，以萬物為芻狗
opened.edition: zh.wikisource 道德經 (王弼本), the 華亭張氏 edition, revision 2354026

evidence.words: 天地任自然，無為無造，萬物自相治理，故不仁也。…地不為獸生芻，而獸食芻；不為人生狗，而人食狗。
evidence.gloss: Heaven and earth leave things to what is so of itself; they neither act nor make, and the ten thousand things order one another of themselves; therefore they are not benevolent. ... Earth does not grow grass for the beasts, yet the beasts eat grass; it does not produce dogs for people, yet people eat dogs.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 5, at [4]). Wang Bi comments on 天地不仁，以萬物為芻狗, the line of the key verse. His comment carries the reading exactly: 任自然, 無為無造, 萬物自相治理, and the grass and beasts illustration (he takes 芻 and 狗 separately, which the sentence reflects without borrowing Legge’s straw-dog explanation). Plain sense faithful. entry-check ok.
